Exp1034 Orange G plate analysis

FLUOstar OPTIMA run 151 · 6 October 2026, 10:44:04 AM (export time) · 492 nm · path-length correction off, confirmed by operator

All 96 electronic sample IDs are in the intended wells. The data show strong concentration and volume trends, with small but detectable departures in several fits. The lowest concentration is dominated by variability at the smaller volumes.

1. Sample IDs and blank correction

The raw-data export, fixed-width sample-ID file and original dispensing manifest agree for all 96 wells, including source, intended volume and replicate. The TXT Content numbers also match the expected X1–X96 mapping. There are 72 samples (three per concentration/volume group) and 24 blanks (six per volume). This establishes correct electronic mapping, not independent verification of the physical liquid in each well.

Each sample was corrected as raw OD − mean blank OD at that same volume. All individual readings remain in the analysis, including negative corrected values.

2. Absorbance versus volume at each concentration

A30–A25 are labelled relative to A30: 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 and 1/32. These are confirmed dilution ratios, not the DNA concentrations from the original experiment design.

A30 has R² = 0.9984, but the 100 and 200 µL group departures exclude zero in their pointwise bootstrap intervals. A29–A26 show no clear departure by this rule; their R² values range from 0.9614 to 0.9983. A25 has R² = 0.7942; its lack of a detected departure does not make it a precise calibration.

A straight-line fit is not the same as proportional response. For A30, the corrected mean is 0.3522 OD at 50 µL and 2.3010 OD at 200 µL: a 6.53-fold signal change for a fourfold intended-volume change. Its fitted intercept is -0.2772 OD. These data alone cannot separate dispensing effects from optical/path-length effects or establish actual delivered volumes.

3. Dilution curves at each fixed volume

The concentration fits have R² values from 0.9909 to 0.9994. The exploratory departure rule flags 50 uL, 100 uL, 200 uL; 75 µL shows no clear departure. These are small departures that can coexist with high R² values.

4. Fit estimates and groups driving departures

OLS uses every sample well, with a freely estimated intercept. R² and RMSE are calculated across individual wells (n = 12 per volume fit; n = 18 per concentration fit). RMSE = √(sum of squared residuals / n). Slopes have units OD/µL for volume fits and OD per relative-concentration unit for concentration fits.

5. Low signals and replicate variation

A25 at 50 µL averages 0.0045 OD above blank. A8 is -0.0065 OD after correction; this is a measured value below the mean blank, not evidence by itself of an empty well. A25's 100 µL mean (0.0127) is below its 75 µL mean (0.0185). Blank and sample variation are substantial relative to these signals.

6. Method, uncertainty and reproducibility

10,000 stratified bootstrap resamples, seed 1034. Each replicate resamples the six blanks within each volume and the three samples within each concentration/volume group. Each resampled blank mean is shared across all corresponding samples. The lines are refitted and 2.5th/97.5th percentiles form slope and group-departure intervals. Sample-SD error bars describe sample-well spread; blank uncertainty is included in the bootstrap intervals.

Pointwise intervals are exploratory and not adjusted for multiple comparisons. Three sample wells per group and one dilution preparation limit generalization. “No clear departure detected” means no detected departure by this rule, not proof of linearity. A slope interval spanning zero would be labelled too weak to assess; none of the ten slope intervals does so here. Instrument saturation, physical well contents and absolute dispensed volumes are not independently established.

Verification passed: all 96 subtractions independently reproduced; all 10 regressions matched SciPy (maximum coefficient/R² difference 4.4e-16); 320 bootstrap regressions cross-checked; deterministic resampling and shared blank draws verified. Original source hashes were preserved.
